key_insight: A conductive GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in CuInSe2 bottom cells without extra Cu or Na, enabling strong back-contact passivation and high voltage.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a simpler, lower-additive route to >16% efficient 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells, which is attractive for tandem solar architectures.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation via ion exchange in the absorber stack
Checked the roles of added Cu, Na, and oxygen flow during oxide sputtering
Evaluated crystallinity and device performance of optimized CuInSe2 solar cells
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV.
watch_item: The conductive behavior of GaOx appears process-sensitive, so reproducibility and back-contact compatibility must be controlled carefully in manufacturing.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
